Our building's air conditioning picked the single hottest week of the entire summer to completely give out.
Honestly, it felt like some kind of cruel, perfectly timed joke from the universe.
The temperature outside climbed into the high nineties.
Inside, without any working AC, our apartment felt less like a living space and more like a very poorly ventilated greenhouse for humans.
I tried every trick I could think of, fans pointed at frozen water bottles, blinds shut tight all day, even a damp towel draped over an open window.
None of it made even a slight dent in the heat.
By the first evening, I'd resorted to lying flat on the kitchen tiles, the only spot in the whole apartment that felt even slightly cooler.
Honestly, that says a lot about how bad things had gotten.
By the second day, half the building had apparently given up entirely.
People started propping their doors open into the hallway, creating this weird, communal misery where everyone just sat in their doorways fanning themselves.
My neighbor, someone I'd maybe said three words to before that week, knocked on my door holding a spare fan.
She said she had two and figured I could probably use one more than she could, apologizing that it was the smaller of the pair.
That single fan turned into an entire hallway trading system.
Someone had extra ice packs, someone else had a cooler full of cold drinks, and by day three, we'd basically become a small, sweaty support group.
Someone even brought out an actual folding table, and we ended up playing cards in the hallway that evening.
We all fanned ourselves between turns, laughing about whose apartment was technically the hottest that day.
The maintenance crew finally fixed the AC on day four, and the entire hallway actually cheered when the units kicked back on.
It was a genuinely bizarre thing to witness, grown adults celebrating loudly over air conditioning, some people literally hugging the maintenance guy on his way out.
We ended up having an impromptu little hallway gathering that same evening, using up the ice and snacks people had stockpiled.
We treated the whole ordeal like something worth celebrating instead of just enduring.
I still keep a backup fan in the closet now, just in case.
But honestly, the heat wave ended up being how I actually met half the neighbors I'd been living next to for two years.

We even started a small group chat afterward, mostly for building updates, though half the messages are still just people joking about who's winning the unofficial "hottest apartment" contest whenever the AC hiccups again.
